question: What counts as an error when a driver touches or crosses over an exercise boundary line or cone during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
explanation: The manual states the examiner will score the number of times you touch or cross over an exercise boundary line or cone, and each encroachment counts as an error.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Encroachments

question: Before safely exiting the vehicle to check its position during an exercise (a "look"), what must the driver do first?
choice_b: Set the parking brake and place the vehicle in neutral/park
explanation: The manual requires you to set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral/park before exiting/entering the vehicle to check its position.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks

question: How many points of contact with the vehicle must be maintained when exiting/entering to perform a "look"?
explanation: The manual requires maintaining three (3) points of contact with the vehicle at all times when exiting/entering to check its position.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks

question: On a bus, how must a driver maintain contact when exiting/entering the vehicle to check its position?
choice_a: Face backward while holding the door frame
choice_b: No contact is required on a bus
choice_c: Use both hands on the steering wheel
choice_d: Face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail
explanation: The manual notes that when exiting/entering a bus, you may face forward and maintain a firm grasp on the handrail instead of the standard three-point contact facing the vehicle.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks

question: What may result if a driver opens the door while the vehicle is still moving (not in neutral and park)?
choice_a: An automatic failure for an unsafe act
choice_c: One of the allotted free looks
choice_d: A verbal warning from the examiner
explanation: The manual states that if you open your door while the vehicle is moving, it may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks

question: How many free looks is a driver allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing?
explanation: The manual permits a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks

question: How many free looks is a driver allowed on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
explanation: The manual permits two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing to check the position of the vehicle.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Looks

question: Besides setting the parking brake and shifting to neutral/park, what must a driver do upon completing an exercise?
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to set the parking brake, place the vehicle in neutral/park, and sound the horn to indicate the exercise is complete.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Final Position

question: What happens if a driver does not maneuver the vehicle into the final position described by the examiner?
choice_a: The driver is penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test
choice_b: The driver loses only one point
choice_c: The driver must repeat only that exercise
choice_d: Nothing; final position is only a suggestion
explanation: The manual states that if you do not maneuver the vehicle into its final position as described by the examiner, you will be penalized and will fail the Basic Control Skills test.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Final Position

question: What must be passed before a driver can proceed to the Road Test?
explanation: The manual explicitly states the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.4 - Road Test

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times may the driver stop the vehicle?
explanation: The manual states you drive forward through the alley and stop with the front of the vehicle within the box; you may stop only once.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.1 - Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, what part of the vehicle must be within the stop box without going past it?
choice_d: The front most part (other than parts higher than the door mirrors)
explanation: The manual states you must stop with the front most part of the vehicle (other than unique vehicle parts higher than the door mirrors) within the box without going past it.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.1 - Exercise 1, Forward Stop

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing, the driver is scored for pull-ups, encroachments, and what else?
explanation: The manual states you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments and final position in Exercise 2.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.2 - Exercise 2, Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 2 - Straight Line Backing, how many free pull-ups are allowed, and how many times may the driver exit to check the vehicle?
choice_b: One free pull-up and one exit
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one (1) free pull-up and may safely exit the vehicle only one (1) time to check around the vehicle.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.2 - Exercise 2, Straight Line Backing

question: In Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, what must be kept between the cone and the line?
explanation: The manual states you must steer left through the opening while keeping the right most rear tire between the cone and the line without stopping.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.3 - Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: What happens if a driver stops the vehicle during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking (before reaching the designated stopping point)?
choice_a: The driver receives a warning and continues
choice_b: One point is deducted but the exercise continues
choice_c: The driver must reverse and restart
explanation: The manual states you are NOT allowed to stop, back-up or exit the vehicle during this exercise; if you stop, the exercise will be ended.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.3 - Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 3, where should the driver bring the vehicle to a stop to complete the exercise?
choice_a: Parallel to the outer boundary, prior to or at the cones at the far end
choice_b: As soon as the vehicle clears the opening
choice_d: Wherever the examiner's vehicle is parked
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to stop when parallel to the outer boundary, prior to or at the cones at the far end of the exercise, to signal completion.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.3 - Exercise 3, Forward Offset Tracking

question: In Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, the rear most part of the vehicle must come within how many feet of the rear of the alley?
explanation: The manual states the rear most part of the vehicle must come within three (3) feet of the rear of the alley, stopping in the three-foot box.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: How many free pull-ups are allowed during Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
explanation: The manual states you are allowed two (2) free pull-ups during Exercise 4.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: During Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, what is the maximum number of times a driver may exit the vehicle to check around it?
explanation: The manual states you may exit the vehicle a maximum of two (2) times to check around the vehicle during Exercise 4.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: If a driver backs beyond the rear boundary of the alley during Exercise 4, what must they do?
choice_a: Pull straight forward past the alley entrance before resuming
choice_c: Continue backing until told to stop
choice_d: Ask the examiner to move the cones
explanation: The manual states that if you back beyond the rear boundary of the alley, you will be required to pull straight forward past the alley entrance prior to resuming the exercise.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.2.4 - Exercise 4, Reverse Offset Backing

question: Committing an "unsafe act," such as forgetting to set the parking brake, may result in what consequence?
choice_b: An automatic failure, and the test may be terminated
choice_c: A verbal reminder with no penalty
choice_d: A retest of only that maneuver
explanation: The manual states that committing an unsafe act, such as forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion, may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 12M.1 - Scoring, Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

question: Which of the following is NOT among the driving requirements listed for the on-road test?
choice_b: Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
choice_c: Maintain at least 55 mph on all roads
choice_d: Complete the test without a crash or moving violation
explanation: The manual lists wearing your safety belt, obeying traffic signs/signals/laws, and completing the test without a crash or moving violation; there is no requirement to maintain a minimum speed of 55 mph.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: If the test route lacks a certain traffic situation, what may the driver be asked to do instead?
choice_a: Skip that part of the scoring entirely
choice_b: Take a separate written test on it
choice_d: Simulate the traffic situation by telling the examiner what they are or would be doing
explanation: The manual states that if your test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate it by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1 - How You Will Be Tested

question: What is defined as "unsafe coasting" while approaching a turn?
choice_a: The vehicle being out of gear for more than the length of the vehicle
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: When stopping behind another vehicle before making a turn, how should a driver judge a safe gap?
choice_a: Stop exactly one car length behind, regardless of vehicle
choice_b: Stop where the driver can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead
choice_c: Stop when the bumpers are nearly touching
choice_d: Stop based on the posted speed limit alone
explanation: The manual states that if stopping behind another vehicle, stop where you can see the rear tires on the vehicle ahead of you (safe gap).
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: Which of the following results in disqualification related to turns?
choice_c: Starting one turn from the wrong lane, or completing two or more turns into the wrong lane
choice_d: Turning at a slower speed than surrounding traffic
explanation: The manual states that starting one turn from the wrong lane or completing two or more turns into the wrong lane is a disqualification.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: When approaching an intersection and needing to stop, what must a driver avoid?
explanation: The manual states that if necessary, come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: While driving through an intersection, what should a driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_d: Keeping both hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states that when driving through an intersection, you should not change lanes while proceeding through it.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: During the urban business portion of the test, where should the vehicle be positioned?
choice_d: As close as possible to parked vehicles
explanation: The manual states your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane) during the urban business portion of the test.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.3 - Urban Business

question: Before signaling a lane change during the on-road test, what should the driver do first?
explanation: The manual states you should make the necessary traffic checks first, then use proper signals and smoothly change lanes when safe.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.4 - Lane Changes

question: Once on the expressway, in addition to maintaining lane position, spacing, and speed, what must a driver continue to do?
choice_b: Focus solely on the rearview mirror
choice_c: Maintain maximum posted speed at all times
choice_d: Continue to check traffic thoroughly in all directions
explanation: The manual states that once on the expressway, you must maintain proper lane positioning, vehicle spacing and speed, and continue to check traffic thoroughly in all directions.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.5 - Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: Once on the expressway exit ramp, what must the driver continue to do?
choice_a: Decelerate within the lane markings while maintaining adequate spacing
choice_b: Accelerate to clear the ramp quickly
choice_c: Change lanes to pass slower vehicles
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, you must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between your vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.5 - Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: During the stop/start maneuver, once the vehicle is stopped, what should the driver activate?
explanation: The manual states that once stopped, the driver should cancel the turn signal and activate the four-way emergency flashers.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the stop/start maneuver, what should the driver avoid doing before the vehicle begins to move?
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to turn the wheel before the vehicle moves when resuming from the stop/start maneuver.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: Before entering a curve, what should a driver do?
choice_d: Reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
explanation: The manual states that before entering the curve, you should reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.7 - Curve

question: For a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards approaching a railroad crossing (unless exempt), where must the driver stop?
choice_a: Within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail
choice_c: At least 100 feet from the nearest rail
choice_d: Within 10 feet of the nearest rail
explanation: The manual states these drivers must stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: While any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what must the driver avoid doing?
choice_a: Keeping hands on the steering wheel
choice_b: Stopping, changing gears, passing, or changing lanes
choice_d: Looking both directions along the track
explanation: The manual states not to stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass, what might the examiner ask the driver to identify?
choice_a: The number of lanes on the road
choice_d: The name of the cross street
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.9 - Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: Regarding clutch usage on a manual transmission, what should a driver avoid?
choice_a: Using the clutch to shift gears
choice_d: Riding the clutch, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
explanation: The manual states not to ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.11(a) - Clutch Usage

question: Regarding gear usage, when should a driver avoid shifting?
explanation: The manual states not to shift in turns or intersections.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.12(b) - Gear Usage

question: Regarding brake usage, what is a driver prohibited from doing?
explanation: The manual states do not ride or pump the brake, and do not brake harshly; brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.13(c) - Brake Usage

question: On a multiple-lane road, where should a driver finish a left turn?
choice_c: In the lane directly to the right of the center line
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.14(d) - Lane Usage

question: Which of the following is listed as a "dangerous act" that can result in immediate disqualification?
choice_a: Signaling slightly late for a turn
choice_b: Driving 5 mph under the posted speed limit
explanation: The manual lists rolling back more than 24 inches as a dangerous act that causes immediate disqualification.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.18 - Immediate Disqualification (Wisconsin)

question: Which of the following is listed as a "crash" that results in immediate disqualification?
choice_a: Any crash the driver could have prevented, or contacting any fixed object or pedestrian
choice_b: Failing to use a turn signal for a lane change
choice_c: Exceeding the speed limit by 5 mph
explanation: The manual defines the crash disqualification as any crash the driver could have prevented, or contacting any fixed object or pedestrian.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.18 - Immediate Disqualification (Wisconsin)

question: Which of the following is listed under "law violations" causing immediate disqualification?
choice_b: Making one turn entirely from the wrong lane
choice_d: Driving slightly below the speed limit
explanation: The manual lists making one turn entirely from the wrong lane as a law violation that causes immediate disqualification.
source_note: Wisconsin Commercial Driver's Manual (May 2026), Section 13.1.18 - Immediate Disqualification (Wisconsin)
